title: Chapter 26: The Malevolent 4
content:
Chapter 26

The Malevolent 4

"I would hear the details," Lan Wangji said calmly.

He simply sat there, but the polite invitation carried the weight of an ironclad threat. Nie Huaisang shrank back, swallowing hard, before dragging his feet into an explanation.

"Hanguang-jun, as you know, our Nie clan is cut from a different cloth than the other great sects," Nie Huaisang began, voice hushed and cautious. "Our founding ancestor was a butcher by trade. Where other clans cultivate the path of the sword, our bloodline cultivates the sabre."

This was common knowledge across the cultivation world. Even the crest of the Qinghe Nie Clan was the menacing head of a mythical beast, caught somewhere between a wild hound and a snarling boar.

"Because our discipline diverged from the orthodox sword styles—and because our founder made his living knee-deep in slaughter—it was steeped in unavoidable bloodshed from day one," Nie Huaisang went on. "Down through every generation, our clan leaders' sabres have carried staggering amounts of malice and killing intent. Nearly every single head of our house has suffered catastrophic spiritual backlash, dying in a violent, bloody frenzy. Even the notoriously short fuses our elders are known for can be traced right back to this."

Take Nie Huaisang’s elder brother, Nie Mingjue. That young powerhouse had been sworn brothers with Lan Xichen and Jin Guangyao. Chifeng-zun was decisive and terribly intimidating; Ze-wu-jun was gentle as polished jade, untainted and upright; Lianfang-zun was brilliant, shrewd, and impossibly smooth. The three had sworn their oaths during the Sunshot Campaign, their exploits celebrated far and wide, eventually revered across the realm as the Venerable Triad. Yet right at the peak of his glory, Nie Mingjue suffered a horrific qi deviation during a grand diplomatic gathering, exploding into a blind, murderous frenzy and hacking at the terrified attendees before bursting into a cloud of gore. A lifetime of peerless martial renown, snuffed out in sheer madness.

Remembering his brother, a cloud settled over Nie Huaisang's face, his shoulders sagging. "While a clan leader is alive, their own cultivation can keep the sabre's volatile temper in check. But once the master drops dead, with no one left to leash it, the blade turns into a weapon of mass slaughter."

Wei Wuxian tilted his head, eyebrows raising. "That borders awful close to demonic cultivation."

"It's completely different!" Nie Huaisang scrambled to defend it, waving his hands frantically. "Demonic arts are vile because they feast on the flesh and blood of the living. Our blades don't want human lives—they crave the blood of vengeful phantoms, fierce corpses, and abominable fiends! They spend an entire lifetime bathing in the slaughter of dark entities; if you don't feed them things to butcher, they turn their spite on the living, tearing our household apart from the inside out. A sabre spirit only ever recognizes one master, refusing to answer to anyone else. And we descendants can't just melt them down for scrap! First off, destroying an ancestral blade is pure sacrilege; second, melting it down doesn't even guarantee the spirit inside will stay dead."

Wei Wuxian offered an unimpressed deadpan: "High-maintenance little princes, aren't they?"

"You're telling me!" Nie Huaisang sighed deeply. "These weapons carved paths through blood and bone alongside our revered forefathers on their quest for immortality. They are royalty."

Swallowing a lump of misery, he continued, "As our leaders refined their martial prowess with every passing generation, the problem only spiraled out of control. It went on until our sixth-generation clan leader finally dreamed up a solution."

"The Man-Eating Castle?" Wei Wuxian asked.

"No, no! They're connected, but that wasn't the original plan," Nie Huaisang corrected. "The sixth-generation leader started smaller. He commissioned two iron coffins for the sabres of his father and grandfather and excavated an ancestral mausoleum. But instead of burying them with gold, pearls, or treasures, he packed the tomb with hundreds of corpses on the absolute brink of violent reanimation."

Lan Wangji’s brow pinched in quiet distaste.

Catching the look, Nie Huaisang nearly jumped out of his skin. "Hanguang-jun, please hear me out! Our family didn't murder those people! We scoured every corner of the realm to collect them with immense blood, sweat, and tears! Plenty were bought for fortunes of cold silver! The sixth-generation leader reasoned that if the sabre spirits were itching for eternal battle against foul creatures, we might as well give them monsters to fight until the end of time. Burying restless dead alongside the weapons served as funerary tributes. The sabres' killing aura would suppress the corpses from rising, while the dead fed the blades' bloodlust and calmed their frenzy—a delicate, perpetual deadlock. That grim equilibrium was the only thing that bought our bloodline generations of peace."

Wei Wuxian folded his arms. "So how did it mutate into a stone fortress? Why are the walls crammed with skeletons? And what about this supposed taste for human flesh?"

"Those are all pieces of the exact same mess," Nie Huaisang said, grimacing. "It... well, it did eat people, sort of. But never on purpose! Our ancestor originally built a standard underground tomb, and subsequent generations simply followed suit. But roughly fifty years ago, a crew of grave robbers dug their way in."

Wei Wuxian gave a quiet hum, thinking to himself: Talk about digging your own grave.

"Excavating a mausoleum of that scale is bound to leak whispers, no matter how quiet you keep it," Nie Huaisang muttered. "That crew of grave robbers sniffed around, convinced there was an ancient dynastic vault tucked into Xinglu Ridge, and mapped the site out meticulously. Those lowlifes happened to have one or two genuine geomancy masters among their ranks; somehow, they managed to track the leylines, bypass the warding array, and break right into our blade vault. They dug a tunnel and dropped inside. Men in that trade see rotting meat every day, so they weren't spooked by a room full of corpses. But as they scrambled around tearing the place apart hunting for jade and jewels, breathing warm air over the coffins—every single one of them a young, burly male brimming with yang energy... Well, remember: every body in that room was a hair's breadth away from feral reanimation!"

Nie Huaisang took a breath, his voice shaking slightly. "You can imagine what followed. Over a dozen corpses instantly mutated on the spot.

"Still, that crew had sharp blades and cold nerve. Working together, they actually managed to hack down and slaughter every last transformed corpse a second time. It turned into a bloodbath, leaving the floor paved with severed limbs and gore. Only then did they realize how cursed the tomb was and scramble to retreat. And right as they turned to flee... the tomb ate them!

"The number of corpses in that vault was calibrated with surgical precision—not one body too many, not one too few, tailored to balance the spirits of the entombed sabres. If the robbers had merely stirred the dead awake, it would've been manageable; once the living cleared out, the blades' resonance would have suppressed the malice once more. But those fools had hacked the corpses into useless mince, instantly blowing a hole in the balance! Desperate to keep enough dark energy to counter the weapons, the blade vault... it... it simply sealed itself shut, trapping the thieves inside so they could personally fill the vacancies they'd just created..."

Nie Huaisang wiped his brow with trembling fingers. "With the tomb ruined, the reigning leader had to find a workaround. He picked a fresh patch of land on Xinglu Ridge and abandoned underground burials entirely, constructing a blade pavilion instead. To keep sticky-fingered thieves from stumbling into it again, he sealed the corpses inside the masonry to mask their presence.

"That pavilion is the legendary 'Man-Eating Castle.' Those grave robbers had arrived in Qinghe disguised as hunters; when they walked up Xinglu Ridge and never walked back out, leaving zero trace of bone or gear, locals assumed some mountain abomination had devoured them whole. Later, when the fortress was finished but before the new illusionary maze was fully established, a wandering woodcutter stumbled upon the white walls. Luckily, none of the domes have doors, so he couldn't get in. But the second he scrambled back to town, he told everyone he'd seen a ghostly white fortress where man-eating fiends made their lair. Our clan figured fanning the flames would keep the curious away for good, so we embellished the rumor and fed the legend. But technically... it really does eat people!"

Digging into his voluminous sleeve, Nie Huaisang fished out a silk handkerchief and a chalky white stone about the size of a garlic bulb. He dabbed the sweat pouring from his forehead with the cloth, then carefully pushed the rock across the low table. "Take a look at this, both of you."

Wei Wuxian picked up the rough chunk of masonry, brushing off a dusting of stone powder to reveal a sliver of dull white bone jutting from the mortar.

It looked like a human finger joint.

Everything clicked into place.

Having dried his face, Nie Huaisang sighed. "That young master from the Jin clan... heaven knows what kind of high-grade spiritual explosives he carried, but he managed to blast a hole clean through that thick stone. Though that's beside the point... The real problem is that the section he blew apart happened to be the oldest pavilion we built up there. Back then, our artisans hadn't figured out the trick of layering brick and earth to seal away living breath; they just dumped the bodies straight into the wet mortar. When Young Master Jin blasted that breach, he didn't realize he'd pulverized an ancient skeleton sealed within the masonry. The moment he stepped through, the fortress dragged him straight into the wall to replace the body he'd destroyed... I hike up the ridge periodically to inspect the site. Today, I found this broken stone on the trail, and before I could even tuck it away, that hound came out of nowhere snarling at my heels! That pavilion is practically our ancestral shrine, I just... I really..."

His voice trailed off into pure, bitter dejection. "Any decent cultivator knows this ridge falls under our jurisdiction and steers clear of our territory for night-hunts. Who could've seen this coming..."

Who could've guessed he’d be cursed with such rotten luck: first, an arrogant brat like Jin Ling who cared nothing for territorial boundaries, followed closely by Lan Wangji and Wei Wuxian tracing the path of a severed demonic arm.

Nie Huaisang wrung his hands, pleading, "Hanguang-jun, and you, sir... I've laid everything bare. Please, on your honor, don't let a word of this slip. Otherwise..."

Otherwise, the Qinghe Nie Clan—already clinging to life by a thread—would be utterly ruined, and Nie Huaisang would go down in history as the clan's greatest sinner, without the spine to face his ancestors in the underworld. It suddenly made total sense why he’d rather endure being the laughingstock of the four great sects than apply himself to cultivation, perpetually dragging his feet on sharpening his ancestral sabre. If he became an elite master, his temper would turn venomous, eventually ending like his brother and his forebears: dead in a pool of their own erupted gore, leaving behind a bloodthirsty blade to terrorize his descendants. Playing the useless fool was far safer.

It was a tragic, unwinnable hand. From their very first ancestor, the Nie Clan had lived and died by this violent art; how could a descendant dare reject the foundational path paved by the heads of his house? Every great clan had its pride—just as the Gusu Lan Clan was celebrated for its celestial melodies, the terrifying, unmatched lethality of the Nie sabres was the sole reason they held their seat at the high table. Abandoning their ancestral heritage to forge a completely new cultivation style would take centuries of trial and error, with zero guarantee of success. And Nie Huaisang lacked the courage to defect and study another school. In the end, playing the spineless fop was his only shield.

Had he never inherited the sect, he could have spent his entire life drifting through leisure, just like in their youth at the Cloud Recesses—lounging on boats, painting fans, netting birds, and catching crickets. It would have been a paradise compared to this. But his brother was dead, and no matter how hopelessly inadequate he felt, he had no choice but to shoulder the crushing weight of the clan, stumbling blindly into the storm.

After endless bows, pledges, and nervous wringing of hands, Nie Huaisang finally scurried out of the room. Wei Wuxian sat staring into the shadows of the floorboards, lost in thought, only to blink as Lan Wangji stepped back into his space.

Dropping smoothly to one knee, Lan Wangji reached out to gather the fabric of Wei Wuxian's trousers once more.

Wei Wuxian jumped. "Wait, again?!"

"Clear the curse first," Lan Wangji murmured, his voice level.

Having Hanguang-jun drop to his knees before him multiple times in a single day was already dizzying enough; even if the man was completely serious, Wei Wuxian simply couldn't handle the sight. "I'll do it myself!"

Yanking his trouser leg up in a hurry, he uncovered the limb. The inky rot of the Malignant Curse Mark had consumed his entire calf, crept past his kneecap, and was steadily devouring its way up his thigh.

Wei Wuxian gave it a casual glance, muttering offhandedly, "Well, it's reached the root."

Lan Wangji’s head jerked sideways, his jaw tightening into dead silence.

Wei Wuxian blinked at the sudden chill. "Lan Zhan?"
